results.title: Robo Inc. Launches US Humanoid Robot Integrator; China Spy Law Still Follows Hardware
results.author:
Scott McCain  
 
 
 Published: Aug 10 2026, 4:58 PM EDT
highlights:
RoboStore, North America's most active distributor of humanoid and quadruped robots, today publicly launched Robo Inc., a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company designed to fill the compliance gap left by the Federal Communications Commission's July 28 decision to block new Chinese-made advanced robots from the American market. The company says it will open a 66,000-square-foot (roughly 6,130 square meters) facility on Long Island, New York, expected to be operational by January 2027 — a concrete deadline and a named address in a sector that has historically offered neither.
...
The 66,000-square-foot (6,130 square meters) Long Island facility is planned to begin producing US-localized robotic solutions in January 2027. Between now and then, Robo Inc. will need to hire domestic engineering talent, establish supplier relationships, secure necessary certifications, and demonstrate to prospective customers that its security review process is rigorous enough to satisfy both corporate IT teams and, for those customers who need it, regulatory requirements.
...
RoboStore distributes foreign-made robots — including Unitree platforms — to American customers. Robo Inc. adds US-based assembly, software integration, security hardening, and testing to that supply chain, creating a "global-to-local" model in which the hardware may still come from foreign (including Chinese) manufacturers, but the integration work — security review of data flows, network access, software controls, and application-specific risks — happens on US soil under American engineering oversight. The planned Long Island facility will be the physical location where that integration work occurs, beginning in January 2027.

results.title: ABB opens refitted, state-of-the-art US robotics facility, reaffirming commitment to US customers | News center
highlights:
ABB today opened its refitted US robotics headquarters and manufacturing facility in Auburn Hills, Michigan, which will support ABB Robotics’ global leadership in developing and manufacturing cutting-edge robotic solutions in the US, for the US and the Americas. The expanded facility reflects ABB’s commitment to long-term growth in the US market, which is predicted to follow global growth rates for robotics of 8% CAGR*, as well as the company’s global investment to build Robotics and Automation capacity and create new, highly skilled jobs. This is ABB’s third global robotics factory expansion in three years across China, Europe and the Americas and is part of its efforts to further strengthen its local-for-local footprint.
...
“The opening of our refitted state-of-the-art US robotics headquarters in Auburn Hills, Michigan is a significant part of our global growth story, reaffirming our commitment to industry leadership in the US,” said Sami Atiya, President of ABB’s Robotics and Discrete Automation Business Area. “Robotics and AI are essential tools for companies in addressing critical labor shortages, localized supply chains and the need to operate more sustainably. The advances in AI-driven software and hardware make our robots more accessible to a wider range of businesses, enabling them to increase resilience and become more competitive. America is now the world’s second largest robotics market, and our production facility will help ABB support existing customers as well as new growth sectors across the US and the Americas region.”

The expansion will create 72 highly skilled new jobs in the area and is supported by a $450,000 Michigan Business Development Program performance-based grant. In addition to capitalizing on the unique concentration of technical skills in the community, ABB will provide upskilling and career opportunities to train workers with no prior experience or degree with the skills needed to build a successful career in the robotics and automation industry. ABB Robotics has invested $30 million in the US since 2019 across four locations, opening its Auburn Hills manufacturing facility in 2015. The recent investment in Auburn Hills is part of the previously announced approximately $170 million that ABB is investing in its electrification and automation businesses across the US.

snippets.snippet: ABB today opened its refitted US robotics headquarters and manufacturing facility in Auburn Hills, Michigan, which will support ABB Robotics’ global leadership in developing and manufacturing cutting-edge robotic solutions in the US, for the US and the Americas. The expanded facility reflects ABB’s commitment to long-term growth in the US market, which is predicted to follow global growth rates for robotics of 8% CAGR*, as well as the company’s global investment to build Robotics and Automation capacity and create new, highly skilled jobs. This is ABB’s third global robotics factory expansion in three years across China, Europe and the Americas and is part of its efforts to further strengthen its local-for-local footprint. ... “The opening of our refitted state-of-the-art US robotics headquarters in Auburn Hills, Michigan is a significant part of our global growth story, reaffirming our commitment to industry leadership in the US,” said Sami Atiya, President of ABB’s Robotics and Discrete Automation Business Area. “Robotics and AI are essential tools for companies in addressing critical labor shortages, localized supply chains and the need to operate more sustainably. snippets.title: Oobotic Opens Automated Manufacturing Facility in Arkansas | ASSEMBLY
snippets.snippet: MELBOURNE, Ark. — Oobotic has opened its first U.S. manufacturing facility in Melbourne, Ark., where the company plans to produce consumer products using automated manufacturing systems and AI-enabled production technology. ... The company will invest approximately $6.5 million in the 97,000-square-foot facility and expects to create up to 70 jobs over the next four years. ... Oobotic said the facility is equipped with modern manufacturing systems and production equipment and will manufacture electronic products and other consumer goods. The company cited workforce availability, business climate and state incentives among the factors influencing its decision to locate the plant in Arkansas.
